thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 1777773001 — p99 latency spike on /v1/streaming (us-west-2). p95 ~700ms, p99 ~2.3s (SLO p99 < 1.2s). Error rate increased from 0.1% -> 0.9%. Paging on-call.

oncall_mike: ack — I'm on it, paging SREs. Starting local triage. :phone:

raj: I can see a corresponding spike of 429s from config-fetch service (configstore) around the same window. Example from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z gateway-1 GET /v1/streaming 200 123ms
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z config-fetch client request id=abc123 status=429 retry-after=3
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z gateway-1 stream-tail request id=def456 p99=2.34s
```

maria: also seeing a sudden increase in KV cache misses in the runtime layer — caused extra config fetches per request. Cache miss rate jumped 4x starting ~10:01:50Z. Correlates with configstore CPU on the primary DB host.

oncall_mike: good catch. Is configstore authenticating via the token service? Any auth failures?

raj: yes — token-store is returning intermittent 503s and config-fetch falls back to token refresh more often. Stack looks like: gateway -> config-fetch -> token-store -> postgres. Token-store logs show a short burst of rate-limited requests (429) from our service mesh.

maria: metrics: token-store p95 doubled, p99 1.8s -> 3.2s during spike. DB replication lag small but CPU saturation on primary around 10:02.

oncall_mike: impact summary for now: streaming tail latency spike and occasional dropped streams for a subset of users in us-west-2. Looks like a control-plane DB/auth path cascading to config fetch -> runtime cache misses -> streaming stalls.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started: featureflag fallback patch v1.2.3 -> apply to 10% traffic

raj: quick mitigation proposal: 1) increase token-store rate limit for internal calls temporarily, 2) enable local config defaults in runtime to reduce configstore calls, 3) add short client-side retry/backoff jitter.

maria: alternative is to serve cached feature flag defaults for streaming routes to avoid config fetchs during burst. That would reduce p99 quickly without touching DB. I can flip a runtime flag.

oncall_mike: do it. Maria — push the runtime flag to force local defaults for /v1/streaming in prod. Raj — prepare token-store rate bump but do not change DB routing yet.

maria: toggled runtime flag: command executed:
```
rbctl runtime set route /v1/streaming use_local_config true --env prod
```
Response: updated route config, rolled to 10% -> 100% within 90s.

metrics-snap: after flip (10:05Z): p95 680ms -> 420ms, p99 2.3s -> 1.0s within 3m. Error-rate dropped to 0.25%.

oncall_mike: nice — seems to have helped. Raj, token-store rate bump still recommended to remove pressure on DB; can we apply a controlled increase (x2) per instance?

raj: initiating token-store config patch: increasing internal client limit to 200rps per instance. Applying via k8s configmap rollout now. command:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/token-store TOKEN_CLIENT_LIMIT=200
```

deploy-bot: token-store rollout started. new pods becoming ready.

sre_eli: joining thread — taking observer. Anything I should watch specifically for handoff in 30m?

oncall_mike: summary for handoff: root cause is auth/token-store -> DB CPU -> config-fetch 429s -> runtime cache miss cascade causing streaming tail latency. Mitigations applied: runtime local defaults enabled, token-store client limit increased, client-side backoff added. Metrics improving but still watching p99 target. No customer rollback yet.

product_jess: product note — Support is getting a handful of customer tickets about degraded streaming session responsiveness (two named enterprise customers). Need an ETA to communicate.

support_alyssa: we told customers "we're investigating increased streaming latency in us-west. Engineers are mitigating; will update in 30m." They asked if it's a data loss — none reported, only intermittent stalls.

raj: token-store pods are healthy, new limit patch deployed at 10:09Z. DB CPU dropped ~15% after that patch and token-store latencies normalized. Configstore 429s reduced to baseline.

maria: confirming cache miss rate back to normal. Streaming p99 currently ~980ms. Still slightly above SLO but trending down. We'll keep 50% traffic under local defaults for next 20m while we validate.

oncall_mike: I'm going to keep the runtime fallback in place for now; plan is to remove it once p99 consistently <1.1s for 10m and configstore healthy. No full rollback required.

incident-bot: Incident severity: SEV-2. Attached runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/streaming-latency. Notify: infra lead & product. Scheduled follow-up postmortem.

sre_eli: I will take the formal handoff in 30m. Leaving a short runbook in the thread: - Current mitigations in place (runtime defaults, token-store rate bump) - Key logs and time window: 10:01:40Z -> 10:07:00Z - Affected region: us-west-2 - Next steps: monitor p99, consider DB read-only replica routing or temporary increase of DB CPU if stress recurs.

oncall_mike: handing off to @sre_eli at 10:30Z. Notes: customer comms queued, PM notified, no rollback. If p99 rises >1.5s again, re-open paging and consider emergency DB scale-up.

sre_eli: taking over. I'll keep the runtime flag on and coordinate with infra for DB scaling options if we see another spike. :heavy_check_mark:

product_jess: thanks team — will draft a short update to the affected customers in 15m unless metrics remain noisy.

support_alyssa: I'll update tickets and include the mitigation steps and expected next update window.

oncall_mike: leaving thread. Good job everyone. :tada:

sre_eli: last check at 10:53Z — p95 380ms, p99 930ms, error-rate 0.15%. Marking incident as stabilized; postmortem scheduled.

incident-bot: Incident stable at 1777773600. Postmortem owner: @raj. Please attach logs and config diffs to the postmortem doc.
